title: Cherry and Coconut Cake
description: A wonderful buttery, soft pound cake bursting with cherries in every bite! The flavour is out of this world, rich in coconut. Bake in a bundt pan or loaf pan.

ingredients.notes: divided: 175ml for Cake Batter, 60ml for Topping
divided: 60g for Cake Batter, 20g for Topping
frozen or canned, pitted and roughly chopped

method.instruction: Heat oven to 170°C. Grease and flour your baking pan.
If using a Bundt tin, be sure to grease it very well as it can be hard to get the cake out of such a shaped tin.
Get all your ingredients ready. Sift the flour, and add the salt and baking powder to the flour.
Dust the chopped cherries with some flour to stop them sinking to the bottom during baking.
Start making the cake batter by creaming the butter and sugar until a pale light colour.

Slowly add the beaten eggs to the mixer on a low speed setting, a bit at a time. If the mixture starts to curdle or split, add a spoonful of your sifted flour. Keep adding the eggs and a bit of flour if necessary until all the eggs are added.

Add half of the 175 ml coconut milk (for the cake batter) with half of the flour, keeping the mixer on a slow speed. Once combined, add the 60 g desiccated coconut (for the cake batter), and the rest of the 175 ml coconut milk and flour.
Lastly, fold in the chopped cherries. Make sure you don't overmix otherwise the cake batter will turn completely red and the cherries will go mushy!
Transfer the cake mixture to the greased pan. Bake for 1 hour 5 minutes. If using a loaf pan, cook time is 1 hour 10-15 minutes.
Test if the cake is done by using a skewer — poke it in the middle to see that it comes out clean. Every oven is different and cook times may vary a little.
When the cake is done, take it out of the oven and leave in the cake tin until cool.

Whilst the cake is still hot, using a skewer, prick holes all over the top of the cake, pushing the skewer through to the bottom. Gently pour the remaining 60 ml of coconut milk (for the topping) all over the surface, distributing evenly with a brush if needed. The liquid will be quickly absorbed by the cake.

Immediately sprinkle the remaining 20 g desiccated coconut (for the topping) all over the surface so it sticks to the hot cake. If using a loaf pan, do this before removing from the pan. If using a bundt pan, remove from the pan onto a plate and sprinkle the coconut.
Allow to cool. Store in an airtight container. This cake is best eaten the following day, although it doesn't usually last that long!

notes.title: Bundt Pan Tip
notes.content: Be sure to grease your Bundt tin very well as it can be hard to get the cake out of such a shaped tin.

notes.title: Pan Options
notes.content: If using a loaf pan, cook time is 1 hour 10-15 minutes instead of 1 hour 5 minutes.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Store in an airtight container. This cake is best eaten the following day.
